questions.question: What distinction between BATI and MiST motivated the authors' use of INLA?

options.A: BATI uses only a null score test, whereas MiST estimates a fully Bayesian model
options.B: BATI supports full-model inference while avoiding MiST's computationally expensive multiple integration
options.C: BATI removes variant characteristics, whereas MiST integrates them as fixed effects
options.D: BATI relies on MCMC sampling, whereas MiST uses INLA's numerical approximation

questions.rationale: The paper frames BATI as an INLA-based Bayesian alternative enabling full model estimation without the expensive integration required by MiST's model.
questions.evidence_quote: with the motivation of making inference based on full model estimation, we propose a Bayesian alternative to the GLMM, using the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) for efficient model estimation

questions.question: Which issue with conventional MCMC inference did the authors emphasize in motivating INLA for genome-wide scans?

options.A: Convergence assessment is not straightforward and computation time can be extensive
options.B: It cannot incorporate numeric variant characteristics into hierarchical models
options.C: It produces only frequentist p-values and cannot estimate latent Gaussian models
options.D: It requires all variants to have effects in the same direction

questions.rationale: The introduction cites difficult convergence evaluation and expensive computation, particularly problematic for genome-wide analyses.
questions.evidence_quote: Another concern with MCMC is the extensive computation time, especially in large-scale analyses such as genome-wide scans.

questions.question: How does BATI represent the genetic contribution under its alternative hypothesis compared with its null?

options.A: H0 includes variant effects and H1 removes the fixed covariates
options.B: H0 contains covariates Xᵢᵀα, while H1 adds terms involving GᵢᵀZ and Gᵢᵀδ
options.C: H0 is a burden score and H1 is a variance-component score
options.D: H0 models only population structure, while H1 models only sequencing error

questions.rationale: The stated models retain covariates in both hypotheses and add genetic-effect terms for H1.
questions.evidence_quote: H 0 : η i = X t i α (6) H 1 : η i = X t i α + (G t i Z)ω + G t i δ

questions.question: How did the authors calibrate comparable significance thresholds for methods with different test statistics?

options.A: They used tests on randomized case-control splits without ClinVar variants and derived method-specific thresholds for matched TIERs
options.B: They used a single p<0.05 cutoff for all tests and cohorts
options.C: They converted all test statistics to Bayes factors using the full disease cohort
options.D: They selected thresholds to maximize power in the ClinVar-enriched cohorts

questions.rationale: Randomized cohorts lacking introduced risk variants supplied false-positive distributions from which comparable thresholds were obtained.
questions.evidence_quote: we performed RVAS tests on ∆DIC randomly split cohorts, but without introduced ClinVar risk variants. Hence, significant associations should only be found by random chance and constitute false positives.

questions.question: How many random case-control splits did the authors use to estimate the empirical ΔDIC thresholds in the benchmark?
questions.rationale: They generated ten shuffled case-control datasets and used the median of the resulting thresholds.
questions.evidence_quote: We used S = 10 for model selection in our benchmark study.

questions.question: At 0.5% variance explained and 0.01% TIER in the Iberian benchmark, what pattern distinguished BATI from the competing methods?

options.A: Every method had nearly 100% power for every gene
options.B: All methods had power near zero, including BATI
options.C: All methods except BATI had power near zero; BATI approached 100% for three genes, with median power 55%
options.D: MiST alone had near-100% power while BATI matched burden tests

questions.rationale: The paper reports an exception for BATI at this stringent low-variance setting: near-100% power on three genes and median power of 55%.
questions.evidence_quote: all methods except for BATI show power close to 0, while BATI achieves power close to 100% for three risk genes (median power of 55%).

questions.question: Which methods repeatedly missed BRCA2 at low variance explained in the gene-wise analysis, and what BRCA2 architectures were noted?

options.A: Burden, KBAC and SKAT-O; both missense and loss-of-function versions
options.B: MiST and BATI; only the missense version
options.C: HBMR and MiST; only the loss-of-function version
options.D: Burden and HBMR; both versions only at 2% variance explained

questions.rationale: The gene-wise comparison specifically notes recurrent BRCA2 failures for the three tests in both variant architectures.
questions.evidence_quote: Burden, KBAC and SKAT-O recurrently fail to call BRCA2 (both missense and LoF versions)

questions.question: What explanation did the authors offer for MiST's unexpectedly poor performance on realistic WES cohorts?

options.A: Zero-inflated p-values from inappropriate handling of low variant counts
options.B: A tendency to overfit genes with many benign variants because of INLA
options.C: The use of a single-direction burden assumption
options.D: Its inability to represent population structure in the null model

questions.rationale: The discussion attributes MiST's poor low-VE/low-TIER behavior to a likely low-count handling problem causing zero-inflated p-values.
questions.evidence_quote: MiST showed favorable results on purely artificial benchmark sets( 14), but performed poorly on our realistic WES cohorts, likely due to an issue with zero-inflated p-values caused by inappropriate handling of low variant counts.

questions.question: Which contrast between burden/SKAT-type methods and BATI/HBMR/MiST did the authors observe across the tested gene architectures?

options.A: Burden, KBAC and SKAT-O had highly similar power patterns to one another, while the Bayesian/MiST group varied less between genes
options.B: BATI and HBMR behaved identically to Burden, while MiST was uniquely stable
options.C: All six methods showed the same gene-wise strengths and weaknesses
options.D: Burden, KBAC and SKAT-O had smaller inter-gene variation than all other methods

questions.rationale: Their discussion says burden and SKAT-related tests shared similar success/failure patterns, while MiST, HBMR and BATI showed comparatively smaller differences.
questions.evidence_quote: The performance of Burden, KBAC and SKAT-O varies considerably between genes, while MiST, HBMR and BATI show relatively small differences.

questions.question: What practical benefit of BATI did the authors emphasize for modeling rare-variant associations?

options.A: It can integrate many categorical and numeric variant characteristics as covariates and gains power when these capture functional impact
options.B: It eliminates the need for quality control and filtering by using only raw read counts
options.C: It guarantees equal power for all genes regardless of background variant burden
options.D: It can only analyze LoF variants, allowing faster scans than missense tests

questions.rationale: BATI's flexibility to include variant characteristics is central to the reported power gains, especially for functionally informative annotation.
questions.evidence_quote: BATI leverages both categorical and numerical variant characteristics and strongly benefits from their inclusion as covariates.
